lead: A multi-operand `echo` prints each operand as it is evaluated, so a call that throws in the middle of one leaves the earlier operands already on stdout.
body: `echo $name, ": ", Thing::of($x), "\n"` writes `$name` and the separator before the throw, and the `catch` arm that prints the same prefix again produces a blessed `.out` reading `Hallbeck: Hallbeck: skipped, …` — which looks like a runtime bug and is not one. In an example or a case whose `try` calls something, bind the value to a local inside the `try` and `echo` only once it exists.
